profile.summary: Enigma is a sequence-to-function model for regulatory genomics from Deep Genomics. It reads a long stretch of DNA and predicts genome tracks such as RNA-seq, DNase-seq and ATAC-seq signal at single-base resolution. Enigma-Distilled is the released pretrained checkpoint, a distilled model provided for non-commercial use.
profile.summary_source_locator: ICLR abstract; examples/basic_setup.ipynb: Mapping model output; README.md: Usage

summary_quotes.text: Our model Enigma achieves competitive performance with current state-of-the-art models at single-base resolution while substantially reducing computational cost.
# Default is to load only rna, dnase, and atac tracks
We have provided pre-trained distilled model for non-commerical use

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Enigma takes a one-hot DNA sequence and predicts many genome tracks at once, with a separate output head for human (hg38) and mouse (mm10). The default configuration in the code combines a U-Net with 7 downsampling steps and an 8-layer transformer of width 1536 that uses rotary position embeddings and FlashAttention, with prediction resolution 1. The authors' stated aim was efficiency: a smaller, curated set of training tracks and a cheaper architecture rather than a larger model. The released checkpoint is a distilled model, which GUANinE v1.1 describes as ensemble-distilled. The distillation procedure itself was not in the sources read.

quotes.text: rather than continuing to scale model size and add more training tracks, we focus on architectural efficiency and train on a substantially smaller, curated set of genome tracks

sections.title: Outputs and tracks
sections.body: The human head has 1190 tracks: RNA-seq, splice junction, DNase-seq and ATAC-seq. The mouse head has 258 tracks with no junction tracks. A helper maps outputs to tracks, for example all RNA tracks for one GTEx tissue. Predictions can be averaged with the reverse-complement sequence.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pretrained checkpoint is listed: the Weights & Biases artifact deep-genomics-open-source/enigma/distilled-model:v0. It can also be loaded from a manually downloaded checkpoint file. A result should name this artifact and version and the repository commit; this page read the repository at commit 28123173. The authors report fine-tuning Enigma on ChIP-seq, RNA half-life and translation efficiency, but no fine-tuned checkpoints are listed in the README.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: U-Net plus transformer. Default code configuration: U-Net with 7 downsampling steps, 8 transformer layers of width 1536 with rotary embeddings and FlashAttention, output resolution 1 base. Whether the released checkpoint uses exactly this configuration is not stated.

facts.value: A DNA sequence as a string or tensor; the example takes a 524,288 bp hg38 interval fetched with GenomeKit.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Predicted genome tracks at single-base resolution: 1190 human tracks (RNA-seq, splice junction, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq) and 258 mouse tracks.

run_guide.summary: Build the conda environment at a pinned commit, load the distilled checkpoint from Weights & Biases and predict tracks for one 524,288 bp human interval, following the example notebook.
prerequisites: A GPU that supports FlashAttention; the model runs in bf16 or fp16.
conda. The environment pins python=3.12, torch==2.8.0, flash-attn==2.8.3 and lightning==2.5.5, and installs GenomeKit and wandb.
A Weights & Biases login to download the weights, or a manually downloaded checkpoint file.
Non-commercial use only, for academic or non-profit organisations.

steps.title: Load the distilled model and predict one interval
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from enigma.models import Enigma
from enigma.data.sequences import Sequence  # helper class
from genome_kit import Genome, Interval

model = Enigma.from_ckpt(wandb_artifact="deep-genomics-open-source/enigma/distilled-model:v0")

# Creating an input sequence
genome = Genome('hg38')
itv = Interval('chr4', '+', 82360581, 82884869, genome)
sequence = genome.dna(itv)  # this fetches genomic sequence corresponding to the interval

# First, prep the model for inference
model.to('cuda')
model.eval()

input_1 = Sequence.from_string(sequence).to('cuda')

with torch.autocast(device_type='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16), torch.no_grad():
    preds_1 = model.predict(input_1)

# Get just the predictions tensor for the rna track
preds_1.get_tracks('rna')
PY
steps.explanation: Cells from examples/basic_setup.ipynb, joined in order and wrapped in a shell heredoc. Run wandb login first, or replace the wandb_artifact argument with ckpt_path pointing to a downloaded checkpoint, as the README shows.

outputs: A TargetTracks object in memory holding the predicted tracks for the interval; get_tracks('rna') returns the RNA track tensor. The notebook prints the object type, not values.
